card_selection_guide.description: Which card to use for each spending category to maximize rewards

groceries_us.runner_up_rate: 5% when rotating category is active (Q1 2026), 1% otherwise
groceries_us.note: After $6K annual grocery cap on Amex, switch to Discover if in-season or Citi for 1x miles

wholesale_clubs.runner_up_note: Amex may not be accepted at Costco. Use Discover or Visa cards at Costco.
wholesale_clubs.note: Costco only accepts Visa — use Chase Sapphire (1x) if Discover not in rotating season

dining.rate: 5% (Q4 2026 rotating category, up to $1,500/quarter spend, $75 max earned)
dining.note: Q4 2026 (Oct-Dec): Discover earns 5% on restaurants up to the $1,500/quarter cap, which beats Chase Sapphire (2x UR). After the Discover cap is reached, switch to Chase Sapphire. In quarters where restaurants are not a Discover rotating category, Chase Sapphire (2x UR) is the best dining card. Discover is usable again: its portal is mapped to Capital One.

entertainment.rate: 5% (Q4 2026 rotating category, up to $1,500/quarter spend, $75 max earned)
entertainment.runner_up_rate: 1x MR (plus Amex Venue Collection 10% on qualifying concessions at select venues)
entertainment.note: Q4 2026 (Oct-Dec): Discover earns 5% on entertainment up to the $1,500/quarter cap. The 5% cap is shared across all of Discover's Q4 categories (restaurants, entertainment, utilities).

utilities.rate: 5% (Q4 2026 rotating category, up to $1,500/quarter spend, $75 max earned)
utilities.note: Q4 2026 (Oct-Dec): Discover earns 5% on utilities up to the $1,500/quarter cap (shared with restaurants and entertainment). Otherwise every held card earns base rate on utilities.

streaming_us.note: Amex BCP is best year-round for streaming

gas_stations_us.note: Discover beats Amex when gas is rotating category

transit_rideshare.note: Citi Lyft credit ($15/mo after 3 rides, up to $180/yr) stacks, so use Citi for Lyft specifically. Discover's Q4 2026 rotating categories are restaurants, entertainment, and utilities, so transportation is NOT a current Discover category. Do not route transit or rideshare to Discover this quarter.

american_airlines.rate: 4x AA miles (10x on AA hotels/rental cars)
american_airlines.note: Always use Citi for AA purchases

flights_non_aa.rate: 5x MR on flights booked direct with airlines or via Amex Travel
flights_non_aa.note: Amex Platinum ••••21001 earns 5x on flights booked direct or via Amex Travel. Corrected 2026-10-17: this category previously routed to a card that does not exist in card-registry.json (a fabricated entry); it now points to a held card.

hotels.rate: 5x MR on prepaid hotels via Amex Travel
hotels.runner_up_rate: 12x on hotels booked via aadvantagehotels.com (increased from 10x — 2026-10-16)
hotels.note: Use the Amex Platinum's FHR/THC bookings to also earn the $600 hotel credit. Corrected 2026-10-17: this category previously routed to a card that does not exist in card-registry.json (a fabricated entry); it now points to a held card.

rental_cars.rate: 12x on rental cars booked via aadvantagecars.com (increased from 10x — 2026-10-16)
rental_cars.runner_up_note: Also use Citi Avis/Budget credit ($120/yr) for prepaid rentals
rental_cars.note: Book through AA for 12x miles + use Avis/Budget credit separately

wine_spirits.note: No card has a bonus category for this. All earn base rate. Citi 1x miles slightly more valuable than 1% cashback.
wine_spirits.optimization_note: Large spend category ($3,600+/yr in 2026) — no great option. This is a portfolio gap.

insurance.note: Massive category ($24K+/yr). All cards earn base rate. A 2% flat card would save $240/yr vs 1x miles. Portfolio gap.
insurance.optimization_note: BIGGEST optimization opportunity if a 2% card is added to portfolio

online_shopping.rate: 5% if Amazon is rotating category, otherwise 1%
online_shopping.note: Check Discover calendar quarterly for Amazon/online categories.

business_purchases_5k_plus.note: No held card carries a large-purchase bonus. The personal Amex Platinum earns 1x on general spend, so there is no bonus rate to chase. Citi AAdvantage Executive earns 1x AA miles (worth roughly 1.5-1.7cpp) and is the best available choice for large uncategorized business expenses.

dell_technology.note: No Dell credit exists on the portfolio. Dell purchases are uncategorized spend, so use the best available earning card: Citi AAdvantage Executive at 1x AA miles (Amex Platinum at 1x MR is the alternative).

wireless_phone.note: No wireless credit is available on the portfolio. The personal Amex Platinum does not include a wireless phone credit. Pay the wireless bill with the best available earning card: Citi AAdvantage Executive at 1x AA miles.

everything_else.note: AA miles generally worth 1.5-1.7cpp vs 1% cashback. Citi wins for uncategorized spend.

international.note: Confirmed no foreign transaction fee: Citi AAdvantage Executive, Amex Platinum (personal), and Discover it. Chase Sapphire's foreign transaction fee is unconfirmed in card-registry.json (listed as unknown), so do not treat it as a safe international card. Never use Amex Blue Cash Preferred internationally (2.7% fee).

ynab_integration.description: YNAB-driven offer selection and card optimization workflow

pre_walkthrough_protocol.step_1: Pull last 90 days of YNAB transactions across all linked accounts
pre_walkthrough_protocol.step_2: Build vendor-frequency map: payee → count, total_spend, avg_transaction, card_used
pre_walkthrough_protocol.step_3: Build category-spend map: category → total_spend, primary_card_used, optimal_card
pre_walkthrough_protocol.step_4: Identify recurring charges: payees appearing 2+ months in a row
pre_walkthrough_protocol.step_5: Flag suboptimal card usage: any recurring charge where card_used != optimal_card per category rules

offer_selection_logic.auto_add: Vendor appears in YNAB transactions within last 90 days, OR vendor is a known recurring charge
offer_selection_logic.likely_add: Vendor is in a category where David spends $50+/month (e.g., dining, grocery, gas), OR offer value exceeds $25 with reasonable likelihood of use
offer_selection_logic.skip: No YNAB spend history, vendor not in any active spend category, offer value under $10 with no foreseeable use
offer_selection_logic.always_add: Free money offers (e.g., Orkin $30 back on $30 = free, CNN/discovery+ subscription credits), TurboTax (annual tax filing), any vendor where David has an active subscription

card_migration_rules.dining: In Q4 2026, route dining to Discover it first (5% rotating, up to the $1,500/quarter cap), then Chase Sapphire (2x UR) after the cap. In other quarters, Chase Sapphire (2x) is the dining card, never Citi (1x) or Amex (1x unless BCP for specific vendors). Discover's 5% applies to dining only when restaurants are the rotating category.
card_migration_rules.groceries: Should be on Amex BCP (6% up to $6K) then Discover (5% when rotating) — never on Citi or Chase
card_migration_rules.streaming: Should be on Amex BCP (6%) — never on Plat (1x) or Chase (1x)
card_migration_rules.gas: Should be on Amex BCP (3%) or Discover (5% when rotating) — never on Citi (1x)
card_migration_rules.rideshare: Lyft → Citi (stacks $15/mo credit up to $180/yr + 1x miles). Other rideshare → Amex BCP (3%)
card_migration_rules.subscriptions: Map each sub to its best card. Digital entertainment subs → Amex Plat (up to $25/mo credit). Other subs → category-based optimization.
card_migration_rules.insurance: Portfolio gap — use Citi (1x miles) until a 2% card is added

portfolio_gaps.issue: No 2% flat-rate card for large uncategorized spend
portfolio_gaps.impact: Insurance alone is $24K+/yr earning 1x (~1%). A 2% card would double returns on this category.
portfolio_gaps.annual_cost: $240+/yr in missed rewards on insurance alone
portfolio_gaps.recommendation: Consider Citi Double Cash (2%) or Wells Fargo Active Cash (2%) for insurance and other uncategorized spend

portfolio_gaps.issue: Chase Sapphire base card has limited value
portfolio_gaps.impact: Only 2x on dining (good), 1x everything else (poor). No transfer partners without CSP/CSR.
portfolio_gaps.recommendation: Consider product-changing to Chase Sapphire Preferred ($95/yr) for 3x dining, 2x travel, and transfer partner access
